public.strategy.lede: Our direction for October through December 2026: make Green Goods easier to use, support real delivery, and grow from what communities teach us.
public.strategy.source: Public summary of the approved Q4 2026 strategy, draft 4. Afo coordinates this direction. Priorities describe the work ahead; they are not release or adoption claims.
public.strategy.priorities.title: Delivery comes first
public.strategy.delivery.title: Usability and Tech and Sun
public.strategy.delivery.body: Reduce friction in documenting and reviewing work. Support Tech and Sun delivery, with field feedback and evidence of completed work guiding the next improvements.

public.strategy.integrations.title: Selective integrations
public.strategy.integrations.body: Explore integrations only where they help communities do and document the work. Ma Earth and other integrations remain conditional. A hackathon integration alone does not demonstrate pilot delivery or adoption.

public.strategy.business.body: Make the project easier to understand and support through reviewed materials and focused partner conversations. Keep public claims tied to evidence.

public.strategy.mentorship.title: Mentorship and growth
public.strategy.mentorship.body: Build the relationships and practical guidance that help people participate. Let readiness and support capacity set the pace of growth.

public.privacy.title: Your information, with care
public.privacy.lede: How Green Goods handles information on the website, in the app, and when you report work through messaging.
public.privacy.service.title: Who runs Green Goods
public.privacy.service.body: Green Goods runs this service. Afolabi and Matt monitor contact@greengoods.app for human support and privacy requests.
public.privacy.collection.title: What messaging collects
public.privacy.collection.body: When you use the reporting assistant, the service receives message text, files and photos you send, chat and sender identifiers, delivery metadata, and your choices and consent records. Linking a Green Goods account also records the account address and proof of control. We use this information to prepare and review your report, link the right account, deliver replies, prevent misuse, and resolve support or publication problems.
public.privacy.consent.title: Your choice to use the assistant
public.privacy.consent.body: The assistant asks for explicit agreement before processing a report. Limited intake information is held to deliver that notice and enforce your choices. Send STOP to withdraw processing consent and stop the assistant. Send START to return to the consent step. Send DELETE to request removal of unpublished private content. These commands do not automatically delete your Green Goods account or public records.
public.privacy.publication.title: Private drafts and public records
public.privacy.publication.body: A messaging draft stays private within the reporting service until you separately confirm the exact report for publication. Account linking and agreement to processing are not permission to publish. A confirmed report can publish selected text, photos, account information and work records to a public blockchain and IPFS. Public records may be permanent and copied by others. Green Goods cannot erase blockchain records or guarantee removal of IPFS or third-party copies. Check the summary and avoid including personal information you do not want public.
public.privacy.providers.title: Services that help process information
public.privacy.providers.body: Your messaging platform handles delivery under its own privacy terms. Depending on the enabled configuration, Green Goods may send relevant message or file content to OpenAI for extraction or transcription and to Typesafe/Jev for interpretation. Voice processing requires a separate choice when offered. Public uploads may use Pinata and IPFS after publication confirmation. Provider availability varies by deployment; contact us to ask which processors apply to your report.
public.privacy.retention.title: Retention and deletion
public.privacy.retention.body: The reporting service has scheduled cleanup for pre-consent intake and inactive drafts, and queues private-content removal after cancellation, publication or a deletion request. Removal keeps limited identifiers, digests, consent and operation receipts, and records needed to reconcile an uncertain publication. It does not erase public copies or the messaging platform’s own records. We handle deletion requests within 30 days and explain any information that must remain. For account-related requests, email contact@greengoods.app; we may need to confirm that you control the affected chat or account.
public.privacy.analytics.title: Website and app analytics
public.privacy.analytics.body: When configured, Green Goods uses PostHog for page views, usage events, browser and device information, error reports, and session recordings. A signed-in account may be identified by its account address. Sentry may collect error reports and masked recordings after an error. Reporting, review and account-recovery link pages block session recordings and element-level capture, and hide private link identifiers from analytics. Messaging analytics use message metadata and hashed user identifiers rather than raw message text. The app also uses local browser storage for sessions, settings and drafts; clearing app data can remove unpublished work stored on that device.
public.privacy.choices.title: Ask for help or exercise your choices
public.privacy.choices.body: Email contact@greengoods.app to ask about your information, request access or correction, withdraw consent, or request deletion. Say which service and chat or account the request concerns. Never send a private key, recovery phrase or password. A person will handle your request; STOP and DELETE remain available in the reporting chat.
public.privacy.successor.title: If responsibility changes
public.privacy.successor.body: If responsibility moves to a successor Green Goods entity, relevant service information may transfer with it so the service can continue. We will give notice and require the successor to maintain privacy protections and honor existing choices. We will explain material changes before using information for a new purpose.
public.contact.title: A person to talk to
public.contact.lede: Questions, partnership ideas, or help with your information: reach the people tending Green Goods.
public.contact.people.title: Contact Green Goods
public.contact.people.body: Green Goods operates this service. Afolabi and Matt monitor this mailbox. Email contact@greengoods.app for human support with the app, messaging reports, partnerships and privacy. Tell us what you need; never send passwords, private keys or recovery phrases.
public.contact.privacy.title: Your information and choices
public.contact.privacy.body: Use the same email for privacy and deletion requests. We handle deletion requests within 30 days. The privacy policy explains messaging consent, private drafts, public records, providers and the limits of deletion.

app.profile.help.faq.accountRecovery.ans: Your passkey is what signs you in. On a new phone, choose “Continue with Passkey” on the sign-in screen and enter the same username so we can find your account. This works because your passkey is saved in your Apple or Google account and travels with you. If it was never saved there and you no longer have your old phone, no one can restore the account, so keep your username somewhere safe.
app.profile.help.faq.accountRecovery.que: What if I get a new phone?
app.profile.help.faq.badges.answer: Badges mark Green Goods milestones like joining early, documenting your first submitted work, or supporting a garden.
app.profile.help.faq.badges.question: What are badges?
app.profile.help.faq.changeLanguage.answ: Open your Profile and find Settings. Next to Language, pick English, Spanish, or Portuguese, and the app switches right away.
app.profile.help.faq.changeLanguage.ques: How do I change the language?
app.profile.help.faq.confirming.question: How does a promise get confirmed?
app.profile.help.faq.confirming.answer: When the work is done, whoever is doing it adds proof and sends it for confirmation. The person it was for, or a steward, confirms it was kept. A promise kept through garden work is confirmed when that work is approved.
app.profile.help.faq.cookieJars.answer: Cookie jars are shared garden funds you can claim from when you're a gardener in that garden. Open Garden funds, pick a jar, enter an amount and a short purpose, and tap Claim. How much you can take depends on the garden's limits and cooldown periods.
app.profile.help.faq.cookieJars.question: What are cookie jars?
app.profile.help.faq.dataStorage.answer: Your media is stored on IPFS, and every submission is recorded on the Arbitrum blockchain when you submit it or, if you were offline, as soon as your work syncs. Steward review adds a separate approval record.
Gardens are the places or programs where impact happens. Gardeners document the work. Stewards care for the garden record by reviewing submissions and approving the work that belongs there.
Choose the garden, pick the action you completed, add media or notes, and submit. If your connection drops, Green Goods saves the work on your device. Once you're back online, open Your Work and tap Upload all to send it.
How do I document garden work?
app.profile.help.faq.howToGetInvolved.an: Open Gardens, choose one that matches your work, and join as a gardener. After you join, the garden appears on your profile and you can start documenting work for it.
app.profile.help.faq.howToGetInvolved.qu: How do I join a garden?
app.profile.help.faq.offerOrRequest.ques: What's the difference between an offer and an ask?
app.profile.help.faq.offerOrRequest.answ: An offer is help you can give: a ride, a repair, a workshop. An ask is for help that you or the garden need. Members start either with the + in the garden's Promises tab, and someone else takes it up.
app.profile.help.faq.offlineSupport.answ: Yes. Drafts and submitted work stay on your device while you are offline, including media and notes. When you reconnect, Green Goods prepares your media in the background, and one tap on Upload all in Your Work sends everything.
app.profile.help.faq.offlineSupport.ques: Can I use the app offline?
app.profile.help.faq.onChainData.answer: When your work reaches the network (immediately online, or when your offline queue syncs), Green Goods writes a public record on Arbitrum: the action, your notes, and links to your evidence. When a steward reviews it, a second linked record captures their decision, feedback, and confidence.
app.profile.help.faq.onChainData.questio: What gets saved on the blockchain?
app.profile.help.faq.photoStorage.answer: Your photos, videos, documents and audio notes upload to IPFS, a public network where files are shared by a content link and can't be deleted once uploaded. Only add evidence you're comfortable making public, and avoid including sensitive personal information in your media or notes.
app.profile.help.faq.profilePicture.answ: Tap the profile photo and choose an image. Green Goods shows your app photo first, then your ENS photo, then the default.
app.profile.help.faq.profilePicture.ques: How do I change my picture?
app.profile.help.faq.reviewAndApproval.a: A steward checks whether the work fits the garden and has enough evidence. Approved work becomes part of the garden record; rejected work can be revised or clarified.
app.profile.help.faq.reviewAndApproval.q: What happens after I submit work?
app.profile.help.faq.seasonsAndCampaigns: Stretches of time a garden sets for its promises: a season for its regular work, a campaign for a focused push such as a seed swap. Tap one in the Promises tab to see only its promises. Each keeps its own count.
app.profile.help.faq.sendingFunds.answer: Open Garden funds and choose Send. You can send GOODS (the community token that carries voting power) or stablecoins to any address or garden member. Scan a QR code, paste an address, or search by name, review the details, and send.
app.profile.help.faq.signingIn.answer: Green Goods uses a passkey instead of a password, so you sign in with your device's fingerprint, face, or screen lock. There's nothing to remember. Prefer a crypto wallet? Choose “Sign in with a Wallet” instead. On a new device? Choose “Continue with Passkey” on the sign-in screen and enter the same username so we can find your account.
app.profile.help.faq.signingIn.question: How do I sign in?
app.profile.help.faq.smartAccountAddress: Green Goods gives you a secure account that signs your submissions and approvals for you, so you don't need any crypto to use it. If you already have a crypto wallet, you can link it to your profile too.
app.profile.help.faq.switchingAccounts.a: Open your Profile and tap Logout to sign out. To use a different account, sign out and then sign in with that account's passkey.
app.profile.help.faq.switchingAccounts.q: How do I switch accounts or sign out?
app.profile.help.faq.syncTroubleshooting: First, make sure you're back online. Then open Your Work from the home screen and tap Upload all. Work that needs attention says why under Pending. Your media and notes stay safe on your device until they upload, so nothing is lost.
What if my work won't sync?
app.profile.help.faq.takingUp.question: How do I take a promise up?
app.profile.help.faq.takingUp.answer: Open it from the garden's Promises tab and tap Take This Up. Some promises are yours at once; for others, the garden's stewards decide who takes them up.
app.profile.help.faq.trackingStatus.answ: Open Your Work from the home screen. Submissions waiting on a steward appear under Pending; once reviewed, they move to Completed. Approved work becomes part of the garden's record, and anything sent back can be revised.
app.profile.help.faq.trackingStatus.ques: How do I know if my work was approved?
app.profile.help.faq.walletDrawer.answer: Tap the Garden funds icon on the home screen to open your wallet. From there you can claim from cookie jars and send tokens. Promises have their own icon beside it. If you signed in with a passkey, Green Goods covers the network fees for you; if you connected your own wallet, you cover your own fees.
app.profile.help.faq.walletDrawer.questi: How do I manage funds in Green Goods?
An assessment is a garden's baseline, the starting conditions and goals a garden's team sets. Open a garden's Insights tab to see its assessments and understand what it's working toward.
app.profile.help.faq.whatArePromises.ans: Neighbors in a garden promise each other help. An offer is something you can do; an ask is something you need. Each promise is kept in the open, and the person helped confirms it. Nobody confirms their own.
app.profile.help.faq.whatIsEAS.answer: EAS is the public record system Green Goods uses. Your submission becomes an attestation once it reaches the network (immediately online, or when your offline queue syncs), and the steward's review becomes a second attestation linked to it.
app.profile.help.faq.whatIsEAS.question: What does attestation mean here?
app.profile.help.faq.whatIsGreenGoods.an: Green Goods helps communities name their needs, make promises, document and review regenerative work, and turn the record into support.
app.profile.help.faq.whatIsImpact.answer: Impact refers to measurable positive environmental outcomes, such as planting trees, restoring soil, managing waste, or educating communities. Green Goods tracks these contributions across four domains: Solar, Agro, Edu, and Waste.
app.profile.help.faq.whoCanSubmitWork.an: Anyone who has joined a garden as a gardener can submit work. You do not need to be technical; you just need clear evidence of what happened.
app.profile.help.faq.workDeclined.answer: A decline isn't the end. A steward may send work back if it needs clearer evidence or more detail. When the work really happened and there's a good reason, add what's missing and submit it again.
app.profile.help.faq.workDeclined.questi: What if my work isn't approved?

public.glossary.canonicalBody: Green Goods generates the docs glossary from its machine-readable ontology and language policy, keeping public definitions aligned with code, copy, and design guidance.
public.glossary.heroLede: Plain-language definitions for the words you'll meet here. Click any term to read the canonical entry in the docs glossary.
public.glossary.lede: Each definition is a starting line. The docs glossary holds the full entry, with cross-references and technical detail for builders.
public.glossary.term.action.body: A documented activity a gardener can perform: the reusable template for work. Each action names what to do, what to capture, and what proof comes next.
public.glossary.term.action.label: Action
public.glossary.term.assessment.body: The diagnosis-and-plan stage of a garden's season, written by stewards and evaluators to name what the place needs and what counts as good.
public.glossary.term.assessment.label: Assessment
public.glossary.term.cookieJar.body: A shared fund where supporters give to a garden's near-term work. Only approved members can claim from a jar, so the funds reach the right hands.
public.glossary.term.cookieJar.label: Cookie Jar
public.glossary.term.evaluator.body: A person who strengthens assessments, methods, and impact claims. Evaluators do not approve submitted work; stewards record those decisions.
public.glossary.term.evaluator.label: Evaluator
public.glossary.term.garden.body: A community of gardeners doing regenerative work in a place. Each garden has its own vault, steward, and gardeners, and its own public record.
public.glossary.term.garden.label: Garden
public.glossary.term.gardener.body: A person who documents work in the field with the Green Goods app, even offline: soil turned, seedlings planted, hours given.
public.glossary.term.gardener.label: Gardener
public.glossary.term.impactCertificate.b: A bundle of approved work, grounded in an assessment and kept as a public record that stays readable beyond any one platform.
public.glossary.term.steward.body: The person who runs a garden: assembling the plan, accepting gardeners, and recording approval or rejection for submitted work.
public.glossary.term.steward.label: Steward
public.glossary.term.vault.body: A long-term deposit attached to a garden whose yield supports the garden's work over many seasons. Endowing a vault keeps the principal in place.
public.glossary.term.vault.label: Vault
public.glossary.term.work.body: One action carried out by a gardener, captured with a photo and description, and recorded as a work attestation when submitted. Approval is a separate record.
public.glossary.term.work.label: Work
public.glossary.title: Words the public record uses.

public.passport.reading.sources: Nothing here is simulated. Where a source could not be read, or is not read yet, the page says so instead of showing a number.

public.passport.vouchers.pool.source: Read directly from the voucher and its exchange pool on Gnosis, as they stood a few minutes before the time this page was opened. What a pool holds, the most it may hold and what is outstanding are three different facts. An outstanding voucher is a claim on a service the garden still has to give. It is not a service delivered. What a pool holds and what is outstanding are shown only while the voucher has moved between the garden and the pool and nowhere else.

public.reporting.help.faq.page.answer: It finishes a step you started in chat. It shows exactly what will be published and asks you to sign it with your own wallet or passkey. Nothing is signed until you choose to.

public.reporting.help.faq.cost.question: Does signing cost anything?
public.reporting.help.faq.cost.answer: Showing the account is yours costs nothing: it is a signed message, not a payment. Publishing with a passkey costs you nothing either, because Green Goods covers the network fee. With a wallet, your wallet shows the fee before you approve.
public.reporting.help.faq.change.answer: No. Once it is published it can't be edited or removed. If something looks wrong, don't sign: go back to your chat and fix it there first.
public.reporting.help.faq.permission.ans: It lets the assistant publish the reports you confirm in chat, inside the limits shown on the page: the dates, the number of publications and the spending cap. You can remove it at any time with Manage Permissions.
public.reporting.help.faq.signOut.questi: Does signing out disconnect my chat?
public.reporting.help.faq.signOut.answer: No. Signing out only affects this browser. To disconnect your chat from your account, send DISCONNECT in the chat. To remove a permission you approved, use Manage Permissions.

public.contact.deletion.title: Request account deletion
public.contact.deletion.body: Ask us to remove your account information and the off-chain data Green Goods and its providers hold about you. Afolabi and Matt handle requests within 30 days and may ask you to confirm control of the account. Public blockchain records cannot be erased, and independent copies of public files may remain. Review the privacy policy before sending your request. Never send a password, private key or recovery phrase.
public.contact.report.title: Report a concern
public.contact.report.body: Email the public work or listing link and describe the concern. Afolabi and Matt monitor this mailbox and will reply to acknowledge your report and explain the next step. public.terms.title: Share work with care
public.terms.lede: The rules for contributing work, photos, audio and text to Green Goods.
public.terms.public.title: Know what becomes public
public.terms.public.body: Files uploaded from the Green Goods App or the Green Goods Hub go to public IPFS, and submitted work records go to a public blockchain. Steward approval controls the website listing; it does not make an uploaded file private. Messaging drafts stay private in the reporting service until you separately confirm the exact report for publication. Public records and files may be copied and may remain permanently.
public.terms.permission.title: Share only what you have permission to share
public.terms.permission.body: Describe real work truthfully. Share only material you own or have permission to publish, and obtain permission from every identifiable adult shown. Do not upload identifiable children or sensitive personal information, including private home addresses, identity documents, passwords, private keys or recovery phrases. Crop or obscure people and private details before choosing a file.
public.terms.content.title: Content that is not allowed
public.terms.content.body: Do not post abuse, harassment, hate, threats, sexual content or exploitation, unlawful content, fraud, spam, or material that infringes another person’s rights. Do not impersonate someone or submit misleading evidence of work.
public.terms.review.title: Review and concerns
public.terms.review.body: Garden stewards review submitted work and may decline it. To report harmful content or behavior, use Report a Concern in Profile Help or on the Contact page. Include the public record link and describe the concern. Afolabi and Matt monitor contact@greengoods.app, acknowledge reports and explain the next step. Reporting does not automatically hide or erase a public record.
public.terms.deletion.title: Removal and its limits
public.terms.deletion.body: Use Request Account Deletion in Profile Help or on the Contact page to ask for removal of information Green Goods and its providers hold off chain. Afolabi and Matt handle deletion requests within 30 days and explain what must remain. Blockchain history cannot be erased. Removing a Green Goods listing or its own files or IPFS pins cannot remove independent copies. The privacy policy explains these limits.
public.terms.acceptance.title: Your agreement
public.terms.acceptance.body: Review these rules the first time you sign in after a new version is published. You can skip and keep browsing. Before you upload, agree to the current rules. The app remembers the agreement for this account in this browser. Submitted work keeps the version and acceptance time in its metadata.
